requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation in `requirements.index.chapter`.

**Directive syntax: standalone, empty body, at least three colons, closing fence at least as long as the opening fence**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` accepts a `::::` opening with a `::::` closing fence and with a longer `:::::` closing fence. It checks the exact byte range of the match.
- It rejects an opening with no closing fence, a non-empty body (`Unexpected.`), and a closing fence shorter than the opening (`::::` opened, `:::` closed).
- It ignores a two-colon form, an inline `Inline :::{requirements-index}`, a marker inside a code fence, and a marker inside a `{req}` example block. These are the "standalone" boundary cases.

**No more than one directive per book**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two markers in two different chapters. It also covers two markers in one chapter. Both cases assert an error containing "only one".

**Index lists all requirements in rendered chapters, each linking to its detail page**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` checks that each of the five requirements has a table row. Each row starts with a link to `requirements-index/requirements.core.<name>.html`. The test also asserts the state column for each row.
- The generated detail pages are checked against the `detail_pages` requirement, which this requirement cites.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers definitions in a nested child chapter. It also covers examples and dotted names, with links to `requirements-index/rules.cli%2Emdbook.html` and `../requirements-index/rules.child.nested.html`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` checks definitions across several chapters in book order.

**The directive is replaced by the table**
- The explicit-directive tests assert that `{requirements-index}` no longer appears in the index chapter content, and that the table rows are present.
- `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` asserts that the explicit index keeps its placement (`book.items.len() == 3`) and that no default chapter is appended.

**Without a directive, the default chapter is generated (`requirements.index.chapter.default`, cited)**
- `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` checks the chapter's title and path, and that it is top-level with no source path. It checks the section number is 3 after a numbered chapter `[2]`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers a book with no definitions and no numbered chapters. It asserts the chapter is appended with number `[1]`, the `| Definition | Evidence |` table header, and `source_path` of `None`. It also covers the prose-only case, where a literal marker in a code block is left unchanged.

No obligation, boundary or failure case that the text names is left without a test and an assertion on its outcome. I found no gap and no marking gap.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
